note: Mission-fit table (F8A Task 10 2026-10-16, extended by F8B 2026-10-17, closed by F8C 2026-10-17): hand-transcribed from F3 section 4, one row per chapter. A 'filled' row has a start, a first-action point and a cruise speed in world terms and is checked by tests/sim/missionFit.test.ts against the real site layout within `ceilingS` at 1x; all twelve rows are filled. A row with `recovery` also checks the flight home to the nearest named field that is LEGAL in the window the chapter plays in (held by the player's side and serviceable, F3 section 2) against F3's recovery budget; `withinM` is F3's own range where it gives one. A failing row is a finding to report, never to tune (Mark, 2026-10-16): it carries `expectFail`, and the test asserts it still fails that check. Every constant (cruise, taxi, roll, landing allowance) and every start or first-action point F3 does not locate is an ESTIMATE or INVENTED, labeled in its row. F8C rows (A1-A5, J2, J4) start on the Essex's deck, afloat, over the ridge or over the sea, where F3 gives no geometry: their start, first-action and carrier points are INVENTED and labeled so, and J2's and J4's starts were chosen to match F3's stated timing (as J5's was), so those two rows prove reachability, not travel time. Cruise speeds are about 0.7 of each airframe's reference top speed (ESTIMATE); deck, water-run and line-up times and landing allowances are ESTIMATES.

expectFail.why: Checked against the nearest legal friendly field (F5C D3: any friendly base counts): Bayug, 32.9 km from the convoy off Ormoc, is 447 s at the formation's 85 m/s (the TBMs set the pace; 387 s flying plus the 60 s landing allowance) against F3's 5-7 min (420 s upper bound), 27 s over. Tacloban, Dulag and Buri are farther and the Essex (69 km) much farther. A narrow miss on invented geometry (the start is read off the terrain's ridge crest, the convoy placed 6 km off the pier), reported, not tuned: a convoy placed 2 km nearer the ridge, or 90 m/s, passes. F10's real points decide.
